description: Checkpoint for the Daily Code Review routine. Records the last commit on the default branch (main) that has been reviewed. The next run diffs main from this SHA forward. Update after each run.

lastRun.notes:
28 commits / 491 files (~20.5k insertions, ~16.5k deletions), the bulk of it the ADS-13xx production-readiness + security-hardening wave (privacy self-service export, GDPR retention/sweep, observability exporters, migration back-compat gate, in-stack maintenance mode, shared @adopt-dont-shop/scheduler extraction, uploads allowlist, RBAC second-wave seed, gateway input caps / LIKE escaping / log redaction / auth-cookie Secure pinning) plus docs. Reviewed in four parallel passes (gateway security surface, scheduler/jobs/migrations, domain service handlers + GDPR subscribers, frontend + shared libs). Overwhelmingly high-quality, well-tested defensive work — nearly every behaviour change ships a test. Filed 3 findings:

- ADS-1332 (Medium/Bug): GDPR retry saga orphaned on publish failure. gdpr-sweep.ts (ADS-1325 #1457) reordered to claim-then-publish; the claim clears failed_at BEFORE publishing, and the publish catch only logs. For the all-services-acked-with-error population (exactly what the retry pass serves), a publish throw leaves the row selectable by neither the retry pass (failed_at now NULL) nor the timeout pass (missingServices empty) — permanent silent stall, no alert. New tests cover claim-wins/lost but not publish-failure-after-claim. Confirmed against source.
- ADS-1333 (Medium/Bug): gdpr-metrics job wrongly behind the cross-replica claim. index.ts added claimRun to the audit scheduler options (ADS-1325 #1457); startScheduler claims EVERY job, so gdpr-metrics is now claimed like gdpr-sweep. But gdpr_sagas is a per-process prom-client gauge on the local registry — with the claim, only the slot-winning replica refreshes its gauge each tick; other replicas export stale values, corrupting sum/max/avg on a compliance-visibility metric. Pre-change wiring was { logger } with no claimRun (confirmed at 9534ec3). The 'harmless idempotent refresh' comment is based on a wrong premise (per-replica, not shared, state).
- ADS-1334 (Low/Improvement): CSRF cookie still on drift-prone Secure check. ADS-1327 (in-range) hardened auth-cookies.ts isSecureRequest to pin Secure in prod/staging vs proxy drift, but routes/csrf.ts:69 still uses secure: req.protocol==='https'; the new auth-cookies.ts comment overstates parity by claiming the CSRF cookie 'already uses' the same check. routes/csrf.ts itself is outside the diff, but the incomplete fix + misleading comment are in-range. Filed at Low (non-HttpOnly double-submit token, needs proxy misconfig to trigger).

Systemic note: both Mediums are edge-case regressions in the SAME subsystem introduced by the ADS-1325 audit GDPR-saga hardening (the claim-then-publish reorder and the blanket claimRun) — the hardening pass added two silent-failure paths in the GDPR sweep/scheduler. ADS-1334 is the incomplete-fix / comment-overstates-parity pattern (mirrors prior runs' ADS-1261/1262).

Considered but NOT filed: forked applications scheduler (already tracked ADS-1330); unbounded scheduled_job_runs claim table (~210k rows/yr at audit's 5-min cadence — real but immaterial for Postgres over realistic horizons, below bar); non-constant-time metrics-bearer/maintenance-bypass token comparisons (theoretical timing side-channel, very low-value tokens); synchronous fs.existsSync per /api request in maintenance hook (on tmpfs, cheap); readiness duplicate 'redis' probe-name collision (latent, no caller passes both); rescue NotificationPreferencesForm SMS-disable lacks a test (toggle already inert); stale JWT_REPORT_SHARE_SECRET grep in onboarding-smoke.yml (dead pattern). Frontend + shared-lib pass (safe-href control-char strip, NATS auth wiring, logger redaction, web-vitals transport, lib.validation .js ESM extensions, ProfilePage GDPR export) was clean — no High/Medium. DevEx/CI/docs commits (#1456 ci gates, doc regens) are other routines' / no-code territory.
